title: W zamkniętym sklepie
title_en: The participle in front of the noun
note:
C1 Block 6, unit 1 (B2-SPINE O4, C1-SPINE Block 6). The passive participle ATTRIBUTIVE and DECLINED, plus THE PLURAL - the two things b2_participle_pass [176] fenced by name in its own note.

ONE IDEA, AND IT IS THE CHEAPEST HEADLINE IN THE BLOCK: the participle is a full adjective, so it takes endings the learner has already produced. Every ending in this pack is owned - dobrego/dobrym/dobrej/dobra from Block 2 of B2, dobrych from c1_adj_pl_gen [186] and c1_adj_pl_loc [187]. NOTHING here is a new ending. What is new is ten strings that are those owned endings sitting on four participles.

TEN NEW STRINGS: zamknietym, zamknietego, zamknietej, zamknietych, otwartym, otwartego, otwartej, otwartych, ugotowana (fem Accusative), zrobieni (virile, recognition only - see below).

THE PLURAL COSTS ZERO NEW STRINGS AND THAT IS THE POINT. b2_participle_pass fenced the plural as 'a homograph inside the paradigm rather than a scope choice' - zamkniete/otwarte/zrobione/napisane/ugotowane/zaplacone were all taught there as NEUTER SINGULARS and are ALSO the non-virile plural. So slide 3 does not teach a form, it names a second job on six strings the learner already produces, on the adj_pl_loc / adj_pl_dat / ktory_plural convention (new job on an owned string is named, never re-taught, and teaches_lemmas stays clean). This is exactly the homograph AGENTS says to keep out until it can be named; this is where it is named.

THE VIRILE PLURAL IS NAMED BUT NOT DEMANDED, AND THE SPINE'S THREE EXAMPLES ARE NOT THE ONES BUILT. C1-SPINE names zamknieci, otwarci and zrobieni. Only zrobieni is here, it is recognition-only, it appears on ONE slide and in NO stage, and the slide says out loud why: these participles describe THINGS, so the men-group form of them is genuinely rare. zamknieci ('locked up, of men') and otwarci ('open, of men' - in Polish an emotional sense) are not built at all, because neither has a sentence this learner would ever say and neither has a taught virile noun that collocates. This is the c1_adj_pl_virile precedent applied one block later, where mali and duzi were dropped for the same reason and logged: a spine example is a sketch, not a licence. The -ni move itself is NOT new - zmeczeni <- c1_adj_pl_virile [190] is the owned example and slide 5 leans on it.

zapisani WAS DRAFTED AND CUT, logged because it is the strongest alternative if James wants a live virile participle. zapisac is TAUGHT (b2_pisac_family), zapisany would follow the -ac -> -any rule the learner may apply, and 'Studenci sa zapisani na kurs' is ordinary Polish with a taught virile noun and a taught governor (na + Accusative, c1_na_acc [204]). It was cut because it costs a NEW LEXEME in a unit whose whole claim is that it costs no new endings, and because C1-SPINE never named it. One word if he wants it.

CASE COVERAGE IS NOMINATIVE, ACCUSATIVE, GENITIVE AND LOCATIVE, and the gaps are lexical rather than chosen. The masculine -ym string covers Locative, Instrumental and Dative at once and is taught in its Locative job; no attributive participle appears in the Instrumental or the Dative because NO TAUGHT NOUN SUPPORTS ONE - kawa, walizka and zupa have no taught Instrumental (kawa was flagged as untaught in b2_which_case's own build), and 'dziekuje zamknietemu sklepowi' is not a sentence. Slide 2's table therefore shows four cells per gender and says so.

zamknieta and otwarta (fem Accusative) ARE NOT TAUGHT, for the same lexical reason: apteke, kuchnie and szkole-as-Accusative are all untaught, so there is no feminine noun a shop-door adjective can take in the Accusative. ugotowana carries the feminine Accusative instead, on zupe <- trunk_want_like_a1 [23], and it is the pack's only -owac participle in an oblique case.

THE -ony CLASS HAS NO OBLIQUE FORM HERE, logged: zrobionym and zaplaconym are both real and both wanted a noun the course does not own in the right case (rachunku, listu, zdjecia and zadania are all verified NEW). zrobione appears only in its owned neuter-singular job and as the named non-virile plural.

NOUN DISCIPLINE, checked pack by pack rather than by eye: apteki is used ONLY as the Genitive a1_gen_ki [39] taught (never as a plural); kurtki was rejected as a plural noun for the same reason, being a Genitive there; kuchni is the Locative b2_fem_soft [135] taught; okna, sklepy, banki, hotele, biura are a2_plural_nom [56] Nominative plurals in exactly that job; chleba is b2_neg_gen [162]'s; ludzi is c1_irreg_virile [201]'s. aptece, listy, zdjecia, zadania, rachunku and nikogo were all wanted at some point in drafting and all rejected as NEW.

FENCED, verified NEW and appearing NOWHERE - not on a slide, not as a distractor: pracujacy and the whole active participle (c1_part_active, the very next node); robiac and zrobiwszy (c1_part_adv); zostac / zostal / zostanie and the dynamic passive (c1_zostac, three nodes on). Slide 6 names the first and the third in ENGLISH ONLY, with no Polish form, so the learner knows where the edge is without meeting the material.

PISANIE IS TEN PATTERN PHRASES, every one two or three words and every one a phrase rather than a composed sentence, so the queue's cloze rule is satisfied by shape and not by exception - the minimal pattern unit for this unit IS preposition + participle + noun, which is the b2_which_case / adj_pl_gen precedent ('dobrych filmow', 'w domu'). No duplicate answers in any stage. Uzycie is ten real sentences, seven with a noun subject; the three that open with preposition + noun carry the fronted-adverbial accepts AGENTS requires.

zrobieni is in teaches_lemmas although no prompt demands it, because the unit does put the string on screen and a later pack must be able to see that it is owned.

intro.title: The same word, moved in front of the noun
intro.body:
Since B2 you have been putting these words after jest:

Sklep jest zamknięty. — The shop is closed.

Polish also puts them straight in front of the noun, in the slot where an adjective goes:

zamknięty sklep — a closed shop

Nothing about the word changes when it moves. What changes is what happens next: standing in front of a noun, it now belongs to a phrase, and a phrase carries a case. So when that phrase goes after w, both words move together.

W zamkniętym sklepie nie ma chleba.

This is the whole unit. The participle is not a special kind of word with rules of its own — it is an adjective, and you finished learning the adjective's endings some time ago.
intro.body_pl: Imiesłów przed rzeczownikiem — odmienia się jak przymiotnik.

examples.en: There is no bread in the closed shop.
examples.pl: W zamkniętym sklepie nie ma chleba.

examples.en: I am going to the open shop.

intro.title: The endings are the ones you already produce
intro.body:
Put dobry and zamknięty side by side and there is nothing to learn. Whatever dobry does in a given case, the participle does.

Four cases are shown here because four are what the nouns in this course can carry. The masculine -ym you see in the Locative is the same string the Instrumental and the Dative use, so learning it once is learning it three times — but this unit demonstrates it only after w and o, where you have nouns to put it on.

Read the table as two columns of the same word.

intro.title: The plural was there all along — it is a word you already type
intro.title_pl: Biuro jest zamknięte. · Sklepy są zamknięte.
intro.body:
When you learned these words you learned zamknięte as the neuter singular, and that is what it was: Biuro jest zamknięte.

The same string is also the plural — for everything that is not a group of men. So Sklepy są zamknięte and Okna są otwarte need no new form from you at all; they need you to accept that one word is doing two jobs.

This was held back deliberately when the participles were first taught, because a form that means two things is worth meeting once, with both meanings named, rather than twice by accident.

In front of a noun it behaves the same way: zamknięte sklepy, otwarte banki.
intro.body_pl: -e: rodzaj nijaki w liczbie pojedynczej i liczba mnoga.

intro.title: In the plural the oblique ending is -ych, which Block 2 gave you
intro.body:
The plural has one ending for the Genitive and the Locative alike, and you produced it for four units at the start of this level: dobrych, nowych, małych, dużych.

The participle takes the same one.

dużo zamkniętych sklepów — a lot of closed shops
w zamkniętych sklepach — in the closed shops

Both words in the phrase move, exactly as they did with dobrych. The quantity word or the preposition decides the case; the ending on the participle is then not a choice.
intro.body_pl: Liczba mnoga: -ych po dużo i po w.

examples.en: There are a lot of closed shops in the centre.
examples.pl: W centrum jest dużo zamkniętych sklepów.

examples.en: There are no people in the closed shops.
examples.pl: W zamkniętych sklepach nie ma ludzi.

examples.en: I do not like closed shops.
In the open shops there is bread.

intro.title: The men-group form exists, and you will almost never need it
intro.body:
The plural splits the way you learned in Block 2: one form for a group that includes a man, another for everything else. The participle splits too, and the men-group ending is the -i you already met on zmęczeni.

zrobione — everything else
zrobieni — a group with a man in it

Here is the honest part. The participles in this course describe things: shops, offices, letters, soup, bills. Things are never a group of men. So you can read zrobieni and know what it is, and you are not asked to produce it anywhere in this unit — there is no sentence in your Polish that wants it yet.

What is worth keeping is the shape, because it is the same one you already make: zmęczony → zmęczeni, zrobiony → zrobieni.
intro.body_pl: Forma męskoosobowa: -eni. Rzadka przy tych imiesłowach.

headers: Group with a man in it

intro.title: Where the edge is
intro.body:
Two limits, both deliberate.

First: every participle in this unit is the done-to kind. The shop was closed by somebody; the soup was cooked by somebody. Polish also has a participle for the one who is doing the acting — the working doctor, the reading student — and that is the next unit, not this one.

Second: everything here still describes how things stand. Sklep jest zamknięty tells you the state of the shop, not the moment somebody closed it. Polish has a second way of saying it that puts the closing itself on stage, and it needs a verb you have not met. It arrives later in this block.

So for now: a done-to participle, in front of a noun or after jest, agreeing in gender, number and case — and no new ending anywhere in it.

examples.en: The chemist's is near the closed bank.
The cat is in the closed kitchen.
The banks are closed, but the shops are open.
examples.pl: Banki są zamknięte, ale sklepy są otwarte.

quiz.explain: w puts the phrase in the Locative, so the participle takes -ym — the same ending dobry takes in w dobrym sklepie.
do demands the Genitive, and sklepu is already in it. The word in front has to follow.
apteka is feminine, so the Genitive ending is -ej. otwartego is the masculine form of the same case.
Feminine again, and the feminine uses one string -ej for the Genitive and the Locative alike.
The plural, and it is the string you already type for the neuter singular. One word, two jobs.
dużo takes the Genitive plural, so both words move — exactly as in dużo dobrych filmów.
Same string as the last item, different case: the plural Locative is -ych too, which is why sklepach can sit beside it without anything else changing.
zupę is an object, so the Accusative — and the feminine Accusative ending is -ą, the one dobrą has.
biuro is neuter, so -e. Here it is the singular; the plural of the same word looks identical.
blisko is a Genitive trigger, the same one you have had since A1 in blisko apteki.
Plural, and banki is not a group of men, so it is the -e form.
The Locative once more. Only the shop is being described — chleb is the object and has nothing to do with this ending.

type_items.explain: do is a Genitive trigger, so -ego.
The plural Locative uses the same -ych as the Genitive.
No new form to make — this is the word you already type for a neuter singular.
